propositions: rebar's LLM runtime contains hardcoded Anthropic-specific logic (provider name prefix matching and feature detection) that prevents Bedrock and OpenAI-compatible providers from functioning with full capability coverage including prompt caching, structured output, and native retry/timeout handling

documentation claims REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL and REBAR_LLM_API_KEY work but _pai_check_config actively rejects these settings, creating a false-documentation bug that blocks OpenAI-compatible endpoint usage

Bedrock-hosted Claude is invoked only through an OpenAI-compatible gateway proxy in the current design, which silently loses prompt caching, tenacity retry transport, read timeout configuration, and native structured output capabilities

the signed verdict sidecar records only a model string, not provider tier or endpoint provenance, making it impossible for consumers to distinguish first-class Bedrock verdicts from best-effort gateway-proxied ones

provider capability detection is tied to provider-name string matching rather than pydantic-ai's ModelProfile abstraction, forcing all new providers to undergo runtime detection changes instead of inheriting capability flags

retry configuration (llm_retry_max_attempts, llm_retry_max_wait_s) and timeout_s do not reach Bedrock at all because BedrockProvider is constructed with no botocore.config.Config, leaving production's live path unconfigured while test paths use direct Anthropic with full retry/timeout envelope
